Description: Calculate the MEAN fluorescence data (Ch2) for infected cells only.
Description_2:

Description: Each Raw Data value will be transformed according to the selected operation by the corresponding Factor, Reference data value, or average selected layout Definition. Multiple transformations can be chained together. For example:
Description_2:
Factor is a constant that all Raw Data is transformed by. For example you could multiply the Raw Data by 100.

Reference is a second selected data parameter (under Reference:) that each row of data will be transformed by. For example if you have the mean intensity per cell as your Raw Data (Y1) and have a second data parameter of the total cell count (Y2) and wanted to find the total intensity of all cells, you would multiply the first data parameter (Raw Data = mean intensity), by the second data parameter (Reference = cell count) for each well (row of data).

Definition is the well layout definition as defined in the Plate Layout Entry. For example if you wanted to divide all values by the average of the Positive Control (µp), you would select 'Sample' as the Definition and 'Positive Control' as the Selection. If you have multiple microplate data loaded and want to divide all values on a single plate by the Postive Control values on that same plate, you would select 'plate' under Grouping.

Chaining Analysis Operations
Data transformations can be saved and chained together to perform complex mathematical operations. Any Analysis operation can be saved using the 'Plus (+)' button. This will add the results of the analysis operation to the list of data parameters found under Raw Data, which can then be selected and subsequently transformed.
